_README: Audit corpus. Disjoint from the six curation papers audited by the sibling submission (DemInf, DemoScore, CUPID, Rinse, SCIZOR, ReMix) and from the reference-distribution sources. Every entry from an external group.
_v2_note: Corrected 2026-09-25 from audit_corpus_v1.json (plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-corpus2-correction.md). v1 stored base_rate as the midpoint of the two printed arms and n_episodes as a per-seed or assumed count. v2 stores both printed arms and the count the paper states. n_episodes is null when the paper does not state one number (n_status ambiguous or unknown); no consumer may substitute a reading or a lower bound for it. checked: human = confirmed against the PDF by a person; machine_reviewed = the Submission Record's deterministic checks; model_reads = two independent model reads agree, no person checked. The top-level _README, _derived_fields_note, _redacted and yardstick blocks are carried over from v1 unchanged, as a record. They describe v1 and the AISTATS study code that reads v1 (claims.py, reference.py and their tests, which are not in this repository). They are not true of this file: v2 has no base_rate, eight of its counts are null, and nothing computes from it except through research/audit_corpus/corpus2.py. 'Stated' here means the paper's stated protocol fixes one count per arm, sometimes by arithmetic over stated factors that n_basis quotes. candidate_display and baseline_display are the names a reader sees: each paper's own name for what it compared, with citation markers removed. The engine, the packet and the Submission Record keep the generic label 'comparator'. Rows 10 and 11 (TurboVLA ablations) became unknown on 2026-09-25 under the strict stated-count rule: the paper states its protocol for the main results only.
_derived_fields_note: Precomputed classification, sigma_star and yardstick fields were REMOVED 2026-09-19. They had already gone stale after the coef_min correction (one claim still read 'erased' when the corrected floor makes it 'inconclusive'). claims.py recomputes all of them from delta_pp, n_episodes, base_rate and the yardstick block, so storing them here duplicated a derivation that can silently drift. This file now holds only inputs and provenance.

_redacted.why: Withheld under OVERLAP_REGISTER.md: these are retraining-noise magnitudes, which belong to a sibling submission under review. Everything the published pages compute from this corpus is present. The unredacted file is in the research repository.

yardstick.note: sigma_retrain = coef * 100*sqrt(p(1-p)). THE THREE COEFFICIENTS ARE NO LONGER STORED HERE. They are derived at import time by claims.py from reference.coefficient_band(), which computes them from the external cells in reference_sources.json. They used to be typed into this file, and because nothing cross-checked them they drifted from the cells: the typed minimum was 0.020 against a true 0.01941, and the typed maximum was 0.158 against a true 0.18566, because the two positive cells of forensic2609 had been missed when the list was assembled by hand. tests/test_claims.py asserts that no coefficient literal returns to this file.
yardstick.history: Earlier corrections, kept for the record. 2026-09-19: coef_min corrected 0.024 -> 0.020 because the minimum measured coefficient is smaller than the value then in use, which had made the audit harsher than the evidence supports. 2026-09-19, later: the whole block was removed in favour of derivation, after the typed values were found to disagree with the cells they claimed to summarise.
